description: The coaching loader fans a single failed lookup out to every kaid, so one student's transient error can deny the whole roster for a teacher without admin permission. ManyCoachedBy runs one lookup per student, then ManyCoachedByActorErr returns an empty map on an error and the loader marks every key failed.

ManyCoachedBy runs one lookup per student, then ManyCoachedByActorErr returns an empty map on an error and the loader marks every key failed.
finding.model_authored_prose:
The coaching loader fans a single failed lookup out to every kaid, so one student's transient error now denies the whole roster; consider scoping it per-kaid the way the session loader does. The sibling loader added in this PR states the principle explicitly (writing_coach_session_loader.go:70-73, "Batching must not widen the blast radius: without this, one assignment's failed query would error out a healthy assignment's roster too, whereas the unbatched per-row calls failed independently") and has a dedicated test for it (TestFetchWCSessionsScopesErrorToItsConfig). The coaching loader is the half where that principle was not applied, and it is the half with the worse outcome: a null field versus a 403.

The comment on this line assumes the batch-wide error means the actor's coach data is globally unavailable. It does not. services/coaches/relationships/coachee.go:70-98 shows `ManyCoachedBy` does not batch at the datastore layer — it fans out one `getCoachCoacheePair` per kaid in a tracegroup, and `err := g.Wait()` returns the first error (tracegroup is an errgroup fork with no concurrency limit). `acl.ManyCoachedByActorErr` then discards every successful result (`return result, err` with `result` still empty, pkg/khan/acl/coaches.go:112-118); this loader copies that one error into all `len(kaids)` slots; and `isActorCoachOrAdminBatched` (acls.go:120-124) logs it, gets `coached=false` for all, and falls through to `actorIsProgressViewingAdminForUser`, which a plain teacher fails.

Before this PR the same event denied exactly one row: `acl.IsCoachedByActor` ran per kaid against coaches' `IsCoachedBy`, a single key query (coachee.go:101-108) with its own request-cache entry. The happy-path win is unaffected by falling back per-kaid on error, since the fallback only runs when the batch already failed.

One caveat on the precedent: services/progress/resolvers/coaching_loader.go:38-45 does the identical all-keys fan-out, so this shape is the existing repo pattern for a batched coach check and a per-kaid fallback would diverge from it — worth deciding deliberately rather than treating it as an oversight.
finding.summary: The coaching loader fans a single failed lookup out to every kaid, so one student's transient error now denies the whole roster; scope it per-kaid the way the session loader does.
